text:
Max Jones has no points in 11 games, and he has been in and out of Edmonton's lineup, with one appearance since Nov. 9. When he plays it's fourth-line work, a little over 8 minutes a night.

The zeros say more about luck than about his play. His own chances add up to 0.95 individual expected goals (the quality of his shots), about a goal's worth, without one going in. With him on the ice the Oilers have scored 4.3 fewer goals than their chances deserve, a big gap for so few minutes. Their share of the five-on-five expected goals with him out there is 44%, a couple of points under the team without him, which is fine for a depth forward.

Evolving-Hockey's read last season put his value in defense, with opponents' chances down when he played (93rd percentile), though over a small 175 minutes. He's quick, too: top speed in the 92nd percentile by NHL EDGE. A 28-year-old former Ducks first-rounder, he isn't going to drive a line. The question is whether he gets enough games for the bounces to turn.
